description.narrative:
Sida tillsammans med EU (genom delegerad finansiering till Sida) stödjer stärkandet av kapaciteten hos Kambodjas skatteverk, General Department of Taxation, GDT. Svenska Skatteverket, SKV, genomför projektet tillsammans med GDT, "Cooperation Agreement between General Department of Taxation and the Swedish Tax Agency” i Kambodja under perioden 2020-2022.
Insatsen syftar till att modernisera det nationella systemet för inhemsk skattehantering för att svara på förändrade socioekonomiska förhållanden i Kambodja med fokus på följande områden: 1) Risk- och kontanthantering; 2) Tjänster för skattebetalare; 3) Personlig inkomstskatt (PIT) och kapitalvinstskatt (CGT); 4) Strategiska skattefrågor kopplade till små, medelstora och stora företag och; 5) Forum för skattesystemreformfrågor.
Stödet till GDT är en del av den andra fasen av en större finansiering från Sida/EU (Partnership for Accountability and Transparency, PAT II, GD-beslut 2019-003682) som har som delmål att stärka efterfrågan på och tillgången till ansvarsutkrävande i den offentliga sektorn genom institituionell kapacitetsutveckling.
Den totala budgeten finansierad av Sida/EU är SEK 14 600 000.

Sida together with the EU (through delegated funding) are financing a capacity suppport to the General Department of Taxation in Cambodia. The support is implemented by the Swedish Tax Agency, STA, through the project named "Cooperation Agreement between the General Department of Taxation and the Swedish Tax Agency" in Cambodia during the period 2020-2022.
The intervention aims to modernize the domestic revenue collection system to respond to the changing socio-economic environment focusing on the following areas: 1) Risk Management and Cash Sector; 2) Taxpayer Service; 3) Personal Income Tax and Capital Gain; 4) Small, Medium and Large Taxpayer strategic issues and; 5) Forum for Tax System Reform issues.
The support is part of the second phase of the Sida/EU financed programme PAT II (Partnership for Accountability and Transparency, GD decision 2019-003682). PAT is to strengthen demand for and supply of public transparency and accountability through institutional capacity development.
The total budget of the intervention, financed by Sida/EU is SEK 14 600 000.

The intervention forms one part of the Partnership for Accountability and Transparency (PAT) II programme. The PAT programme aims to complement EU's sector budget support to the PFM reform with the objective to facilitate "an enabling environment for the PFM reform by strengthened demand for and supply of public transparency and accountability through institutional capacity development". The overall objective for the intervention in the area of revenue mobilization is "to modernize the domestic revenue collection system to respond to the changing socio-economic environment (RMS II)". GDT and STA will collaborate in four different components and a fifth component will also involve Department of Economic Policy within MEF. The expected outcomes per component are: Component 1: Risk Management and Cash Sector: - GDT works in a structured way with prioritised voluntary compliance and risks supporting fair competition - Increased knowledge experience within GDT about how Compliance Risk Management - on strategic as well as operational level - can enhance taxpayer compliance Component 2: Taxpayer Service - Taxpayers in Cambodia are in general satisfied with the interaction with GDT in order to get service/information - Increased experience and strengthened knowledge within GDT about how taxpayer services contribute to increased voluntary compliance by improved information and transparency Component 3: Personal Income Tax (PIT) and Capital Gains Tax (CGT) - Concerned citizens of Cambodia are filing CGT Component 4: Small, Medium and Large taxpayers – strategic issues - Increased experience and strengthened knowledge about the taxpayers' perception of their buisness processes and how tax administration can support their voluntary compliance for a fair and growing economy is used in GDT's planning Component 5: Forum for Tax System Reform Issues - Increased cooperation between MEF and GDT in Tax System Reform matters

The objective of the project has been to improve the General Department of Taxations capacity and contribute to a transformation to become a modern and more efficient and effective revenue administration. On an outcome level for the whole project period the following are some achievements noted from the final report:
GDT has with the support of the Swedish Tax Agency, STA, launched a new and more modern and taxpayer oriented website. An external survey on the culture of paying tax, knowledge, perception and attitude toward tax, was conducted in 2017 by Kantar as a baseline and in 2022 a follow-up survey was done by CDRI (Cambodian Development Research Institute). The results show that the tax payers now have more trust in GDT than before and that they think it is easier to comply with tax regulations. GDT argues that the development of the website has contributed to this improved attitude among taxpayers.
Additionally, several performed activities to enhance the level of knowledge and experience among the staff of GDT is probably another reason for the noticeably enhanced taxpayer satisfaction, according to the follow-up survey. The project has conducted several workshops regarding what a Taxpayer Service Strategy is and why it contributes to more efficient service-giving and voluntary compliance. Work has led to the internal understanding and agreement on that the strategy has an important place in securing one-voice when it comes to external communications and services. It has also been key to carry out preventive activities by enhancing a tax culture and knowledge about taxes and the tax system. GDT has finalized its first Taxpayer Service Strategy for the segment Small businesses and started on the segment Future taxpayers.
GDT has with support from STA been working on preparing the implementation of Capital Gains Tax, CGT. The CGT was planned to start in 2020 but the implementation was later postponed to the beginning of 2024. It has therefore not been possible for STA to assist and follow up on the introduction of the tax during the project duration. Instead, STAs experts have assisted the GDT working team in various areas to be fully prepared for the actual implementation. STA has assisted with, types of regulation, work processes, forms, education and communications. During the initial discussions on the design of the personal income tax, PIT, which also was to be introduced during the duration of this project, discussions were held on joint taxation between spouses. STA advised against such taxation system since it has a negative impact on gender equality. At present, there is no proposal for joint taxation between spouses, to be introduced in Cambodia. GDT is fully prepared through the project to manage the introduction of the PIT when the decision for its start has been taken by MEF.
GDT has gained competence and learned methods and techniques for selection of compliance activities and methods and techniques for evaluating the effectiveness of the activities. GDT has started to work with development of guidelines (and guides) for simplified tax procedures (both external and internal procedures) concerning compliance activities and auditing. This all together ensures that there is a full circle of comprehensive risk management approach within GDT. Everything from assessing general risks to evaluating compliance activities and adding knowledge for the next iteration of GRO.
GDT have also enhanced its knowledge in audit methods and activities directly linked to the outcome of RAR (Risk Area Report) and how to select the objects for auditing.
STA has helped to build-up capacity among GDT and GDP staff for conducting future tax gap estimations. Participants have gained a better understanding of the benefits and costs of both top-down and bottom-up methods and which tax gaps are typically estimated using different methods. By the use of examples the GDT and GDP have developed practical knowledge on how to use simple top-down methods in tax gap analysis, including problems and pitfalls that might occur.
Exemple of results divided over the components:
The project has been divided into five components, Risk Management and Cash Sector, Small, medium and Large Taxpayer Strategic Issues, Taxpayer Service, Personal Income Tax (PIT)/Capital Gains Tax (CGT) and a fifth component; Forum on Tax System Reform. However, during the three year period there has been some adjustments within the components.
Main results:
Risk Management and cash sector
By the end of the activity period the GRO has been revised and updated by GDT. GDT now have the knowledge on how to work with and use the GRO as a part of the risk management process. The project has supported the GDT in developing and strengthening the CRM-approach but also facilitated the implementation and annual update of the GRO. The project activities has been essential in enabling the GDT to have stronger focus on risk management and consequently to devote its resources towards measures and activities that impacts compliance the most.
Small, medium and large Taxpayer Strategic Issues
By the end of the project, the risks in the Risk Area Report (RAR) has been valuated in order to work on the most important risks to tackle, sharing experiences and building competences on the Selection process and sharing experiences to raise competences on audit methodology and techniques. STA has shared experiences in audit methodology and how to detect false invoices. Audit methods and activities directly linked to the outcome of RAR (Risk AreaReport) and how to select the objects for auditing, has been discussed. A draft guideline in two sectors on how to conduct audits has been produced. The draft has been subject to user tests and consequently the GDT has learned how to conduct such tests.The audit guideline will make auditors work in the same way, using the same techniques and that will enhance the trust from the tax payers, knowing that GDT works in a uniform way.
Workshops and digital meetings has been held to improve GDTs knowledge in:
The Compliance risk management process, that is how to identify, analyse, assess and prioritise among risks areas /groups of taxpayers.
Methods and techniques for analysing and evaluating suitable Risk areas/groups of taxpayers.
Methods and techniques for selection for compliance activities. Workshops and training about audit planning, audit methods and activities in general.
The efforts resulted in a developed method on how to work with the RAR and measure the risks wich will help GDT to adopt a more comprehensive risk based approach.
Taxpayer Service
The project has conducted several workshops regarding what a Taxpayer Service Strategy is and why it contributes to more efficient service-giving and voluntary compliance. Work has led to the understanding and agreement on that the strategy has an important place in securing one-voice when it comes to external communications and services as well as a key to preventive activities through enhancement of tax culture and knowledge.
GDT launched with the support of STA new and more modern website in 2020. The websites new structure is a step towards a fully taxpayer oriented website.
In 2021 a draft model for a Taxpayer Service strategy (TPS) was elaborated. The model was shared and discussed among GDT representatives. The model could be applied to prioritized taxpayers (small taxpayers) and to understand the needs of taxpayers, the gap between what we do and what the taxpayer needs; as well as, to close the gap and finding the relevant ractivities and how to measure those activities.
IN 2022 adopted a method for developing Taxpayer Education activities, with the support from the STA. The method strengthens the connection between the needs of taxpayers with the content which is reflected in trainings, education and communication.
The Call Centre has proved to be quite a success. Thousands of calls each year (over 200,000 from 2018) and 99.7% satisfaction with service received (although they still need to develop a way to monitor this and rely for now on things like number of likes on Facebook).
Personal Income Tax and Capital Gains Tax
Tangible outputs which has been delivered during 2021 were the following:
- CGT forms approved by the Director General of the GDT (TCGT 01 and 02)
- A draft workflow concerning CGT on immovable assets
- CGT dissemination (seminars) was conducted with the general public, ministries, taxpayers, tax officials and management across the country.
The activities for 2022 was focusing on work flows regarding CGT (immovable and movable property), knowledge on standard reporting regarding CGT, development of a guide book and a risk management mechanism regarding CGT. In November 2022, GDP has finalized the draft of the Policy framework for the implementation of PIT. GDT has provided data and comment to GDP as input for the preparation of the final framework draft
Forum on Tax System Reform
The project activities have resulted in a better understanding among the participants of the benefits and costs of both top-down and bottom-up methods and what tax gaps are typically estimated, using different methods. By the use of examples the participants have developed practical knowledge on how to use simple top-down methods in tax gap analysis, including understanding possible problems and pitfalls.
Participants of the Tax System Working Group (TWG) understand the statistical properties of bottom-up methods based on random sampling.
Participants have also discussed the methodological problems of extrapolating both random and non-random sampling.
One of the main lessons learned is that the availability of relevant data and engagement of relevant government institutions is of crucial importance.
The TWG has discussed different types of tax for conducting tax gap analysis and staff have been trained on tax gap analysis specifically on:
- Concept of tax gap analysis and the importance of the analysis for comparing collected tax and assessed tax/theoretical tax.
- Tax gap analysis approaches (top-down approach vs. bottom-up approach)
- Tools for tax gap analysis.
The TWG has decided to conduct tax gap analysis on excise taxes and VAT on alcohol and tobacco products. For conducting tax gap analysis training in these areas,
- The TWG has requested data from General Department of Taxation and General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia.
- The TWG has consulted with National Institute of Statistics and requested consumption data of alcohol and tobacco products.
2020 is the first year of the second agreement phase of the cooperation between Cambodian General Department of Taxation (GDT) and the Swedish Tax Agency (STA). This institutional cooperation between GDT and STA is a part by the overall Partnership for Accountability and Transparency (PAT) programme co-funded by Sida and EU. The most recent report submitted in February 2020 covers implementation of the previous agreement phase and is therefore assessed in the Completion Report of the former contribution. The first report from the new agreement phase will be submitted in February 2021.
The overall objective of this taxation-project as part of PAT II is to modernize the domestic revenue collection system to respond to the changing socio-economic environment.
Examples of progress and results
1. Risk Management and Cash Sector
The overall goal is to strengthen mobilization of domestic revenue by expanding the coverage of taxpayers and increasing the effectiveness of tax collection in the cash sector. To manage this, GDT decided to introduce CRM in its planning process to be able to use the scarce resources of GDT more efficiently.
- GDT has now implemented a general risk overview (GRO) which is updated yearly. The GDT has raised knowledge and will now be able to update and continue the work with GRO without the assistance of the Swedish taxation authority (STA). GRO is one part of a Compliance Risk Management work. It is important to continue the work and spread CRM in the entire organization. It is important to have access to qualitative data in order for the analysis and conclusions of GRO to be of use. If not, there is a risk that the areas with the highest risks are not prioritized. How can this be secured?
- The implementation of a cash receipt system has not been possible to carry out as there is still no decision on this by GDT and it is not expected to come during 2022. GDT has however gained knowledge about challenges, how to plan and what to focus on when implementing a legislation regarding fiscal cash registers.
= The activities have been concluded during 2021.
2. Taxpayer Services
The goal is to increase taxpayers' understanding and perception of the tax system and their trust for GDT. The component is divided into three parts, taxpayer service strategy, communcations and education, and development of the GDT website.
- A model for a taxpayer service strategy has been introduced to GDT, where there have been trainings and discussions on the model, and preparation for the implementation.
- GDT has continued its work on the GDT website in order to make it more user driven. Several parts have been transformed, both structurally and content-wise.
- Taxpayer education needs to be more relevant to specific target groups. GDT and STA have started activities on a model for defining specific target groups, how to analyze the needs and waht specific characteristics are relevant to each specific target group.
= The component is expected to be continued in 2022 and the aim is to achieve the results.
3. Personal Income Tax (PIT)
The goal is to introduce a coherent PIT in Cambodia, a system with simple rules that are easy to implement for GDT and easy to understand for the taxpayers. PIT is meant to be a progressive tax where the taxpayers must add all incomes when calculating the tax liability. This will benefit the social welfare in the society and benefit the people in the country. The PIT introduction has been postponed by the government. Instead a Capital Gains Tax CGT was to be introduced. However, also this tax has been delayed now to 2024.
Although the actual tax implementation have been delayed, work has been carried out to update the action plan concerning the CGT and its procedures.
- A workflow for processing CGT-cases has also been drafted and discussed.
- CGT dissemination seminars have been conducted with the general public, taxpayers and tax officials across the country.
- The project partners have been engaged in discussions concerning risk management in relation to CGT.
- CGT forms have been approved by GDT's Director General.
= The component will not be achieved as the tax will not be introduced during the life time of the project. However, all documentation and training of staff at GDT will be done so that the tax can be implemented in the future. The target has been adjusted.
4. Small, medium and large taxpayer strategic issues
The goal is for GDT to get experience and knowledge about taxpayers' perception of their business processes and how tax administration can support their voluntary compliance for a fair and growing economy and that this is used in GDT's planning.
This component has had seven digital meetings. Initially, the work in the component was conducted within one and the same working group for the entire component but late 2021 it was divided into three different groups: Risk management, Selection, and Audit methodology.
- GDT has gained an understanding about what modern Risk management consists of and how it can be used by the organization. GDT has also received information on how to write a RAR (risk area report) and the work on writing a RAR in the selected risk areas construction and logistics has started.
- The work to develop a method for Selection of the companies to audit within the construction and logistics will begin as soon as the process of writing the RARs have reached a certain level.
- Audit methodology, will be introduced when the "right" companies have been selected for audit. Guidelines and guides will be developed describing how to conduct audits with the goal to have more consistent (used by all tax branches) methodology of auditing.
= STA assesses that the goals will be reached in 2022. The plan is that when GDT and STA have undertaken this work for both the construction and logisitcs sectors, GDT will have the practical know-how and methods to address the other risk areas without support from the STA.
5. Forum on tax system reform
The goal is to increase the cooperation between MEF and GDT in tax system reform matters. GDT and GDEP/MEF will work together on develping skills and techniques for doing a tax gap analysis, as a preparation for the new tax system reform. The ambition is not to make a full tax gap analysis, as it requires much more time and resources, but to build capacity within the GDT and GDEP/MEF to undertake such analysis themselves, using different kinds of methods and techniques.
During 2021, 12 digital meetings have been held. The focus has been to share knowledge and experiences on the methods used by STA when assessing the tax gap. The STA has organized the meetings in different modules and each module typically describes a specific method for assessing the tax gap. STA assesses that the participants now have a better understanding of the different methods considered to be standard for assessing the gap.
= STA believes that the participants will have the technical competence to carry out the assessments of the tax gaps, which are scheduled to take place during 2022.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
